text: Totems need attention as well as power. A totem you use stays awake; one you ignore slowly goes to sleep. This is called **Keeping**, and a totem is always in one of three states:
- **Answered**: awake, for about **40 minutes** of loaded time after it was last used.
- **Dim**: fading, for another **40 minutes**. Matching stations take about **30% longer**.
- **Quiet**: asleep. New work may pause, even with Pulse to spare.
The clock only runs while the totem's chunk is loaded. A full generator does not wake a quiet totem by itself.

pages.title: Waking a totem
text: Right-click the totem with an empty hand, or use a **Bone Chime** on it. It answers at once.
Drumming a Drumheart by hand wakes every totem within 8 blocks. So do Kin drummers from the tribes, and a Ley Collector whose beat is 8 or more.
Work keeps totems awake: every second a matching station works, it feeds the totems of its voice. That keeps an answered or dim totem going, but it will not wake one that has already gone quiet.
A Heartbeat plate can keep a Drumheart producing power, but redstone beats do not keep totems awake.

steps.caption: This Shatter has Pulse and an Earth totem, but it has stopped: its totem has gone quiet.
Use a Bone Chime on the totem, or right-click it with an empty hand, to wake it.
The station picks its work back up, and every second it works keeps the totem answered.

pages.title: Planning a camp
text: Totems in lush places stay awake **twice as long**: open sky, water and plants right around a totem slow its clock by half. A roofed hole forgets you faster.

The Ley Lens voice sight tints totems gold when answered, dull when dim and grey when quiet. And when a station stops while its power looks fine, crouch and right-click it with this book: it says whether its totem is dim or quiet.
